subject: Sapphire — sudden egress latency and increased 5xx rate (executive sync)
messages:
From: Mike Reynolds <mike@shop-sapphire.com>
To: Sapphire Ops <ops@sapphire.io>, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: spike in inference latency and 502s in checkout

Hi Hannah / Redwood team,

We're seeing a dramatic increase in checkout latency starting ~07:45 PT this morning; roughly 6x p95 and a spike in 502/504 from your hosted API that correlates with a drop in successful purchases. Our ops team pulled a small trace and attached a short pcap — it looks like requests to the inference gateway are sometimes timing out and being retried. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side or if you're seeing errors as well? We have a high-volume sale running today so need urgent help.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Reynolds
Head of Platform, Sapphire Commerce

Attachments: sapphire-trace-20261109.pcap
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: spike in inference latency and 502s in checkout

Marissa / Jonas / Vanessa — looping you in. Customer SAPP-4372 is reporting p95 latency jump and increased 5xx. They've attached a pcap that suggests intermittent timeouts to our egress gateway. Initial checks: host-level metrics look normal but we see elevated tcp retransmits from a subset of edge nodes in us-west-2.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: confirm service-level ingestion / queueing and whether any recent config pushes to the proxy or timeout tuning happened overnight.
- Jonas: please review the pcap and run quick traceroutes from the affected egress fleet to the Sapphire endpoints; flag any VPC peering flaps or DNS resolution anomalies.
- Vanessa: prepare an exec note for the customer (ack + ETA) and check Reserved/Dedicated pools' capacity.

I'll coordinate. If this looks like a network path issue we need to bring CloudMesh partner into the loop.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: spike in inference latency and 502s in checkout

Quick update from runtime:
- No config pushes to the inference proxy or gateway between 02:00-07:00 PT.
- Ingestion queues (per-route) show a brief backlog around 07:46 but drained within ~90s — unsurprising given retries.
- Service logs show a surge of connection resets (ECONNRESET) from a small subset of instances in the us-west-2 egress pool (instance ids: egr-32*, egr-34*).
- We pulled token-level timing: tokenization & model inference time are stable; time is being spent in TCP connect / TLS handshake and backoffs.

I've attached svc-metrics-20261109.csv with per-instance metrics for the last 2 hours. Jonas, looks like handoffs and network-level retries are the culprit.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Runtime SRE, Redwood

Attachments: svc-metrics-20261109.csv
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: spike in inference latency and 502s in checkout

I pulled the pcap and ran traceroutes from egr-321 and egr-348 (both in the us-west-2 egress set). Findings:
- There are intermittent AS path asymmetries after our peering hop to CloudMesh transit around 07:40 PT; multiple flows show packet reorder and duplicated SYN retransmissions.
- DNS lookups for customer endpoints are resolving correctly but TTLs from their authoritative are low (10s) — we observed repeated re-resolutions with slightly different IPs which aligns with their own load balancer rotation.
- No firewall rules changed on our side, but CloudMesh reported an automated route refresh for a peering session at 07:41 PT (see CloudMesh note below) — that aligns with outage window.

Recommendation: open an immediate joint-troubleshoot with CloudMesh NetOps to confirm whether their peering refresh caused transient blackholed SYNs or flap-induced TCP resets. In parallel, consider temporarily diverting SAPP traffic to a different egress pool in us-east-1 to reduce customer impact.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Network Ops, Redwood
From: CloudMesh NetOps <netops@cloudmesh.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Alert — peering session refresh at 07:41 PT

Hi Jonas / Hannah,

Thanks for the heads up. We performed an automated route refresh on the transit session to clear a stale MAC-learning entry at 07:41 PT; that refresh resulted in a short control-plane reconvergence window of ~35 seconds in a single fabric region. We can confirm that we saw elevated drop counters for traffic matching Redwood's ASN for that 35s.

We apologize — we didn't realize that the refresh would coincide with high-volume checkout windows for any customer. We're happy to coordinate a post-mortem and to schedule a maintenance window for similar cleanup outside critical customer windows.

— CloudMesh NetOps
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec: customer impact and mitigation plan (Sapphire)

Team — thanks for the rapid triage. Per the data: the root cause is a transient CloudMesh peering control-plane refresh that caused ~30-40s of elevated drops and subsequent TCP retries that amplified during the customer's sale traffic. Immediate actions:
1) Vanessa: send a short customer exec note acknowledging the cause and our mitigations (diversion + rate-limits fallback) and promise a post-mortem timeline.
2) Jonas/Marissa: failover Sapphire traffic to the us-east-1 egress pool for the next 2 hours; validate that retries reduce and p95 returns to baseline.
3) Hannah: coordinate with CloudMesh to get an incident timeline and get them to commit to no control-plane refreshes during known customer peak windows for the next 72 hours.
4) Ops: generate a credit estimate for lost conversions during the blip (finance will need it).

I'll be on the customer call at 10:15 PT. Vanessa — draft the note and I'll review.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mike Reynolds <mike@shop-sapphire.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, CloudMesh NetOps <netops@cloudmesh.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Sapphire outage follow-up and next steps

Mike — thanks again for the quick signal and for sharing the trace. Summary and next steps: 

What happened:
- A control-plane route refresh initiated by CloudMesh at 07:41 PT on 2026-11-09 resulted in ~35s of elevated packet drop for traffic between Redwood and Sapphire. That caused connection resets and increased request retries which manifested as p95 latency spikes and higher 5xx.

Immediate remediation we performed:
- Diverted Sapphire traffic to our us-east-1 egress pool within 10 minutes of detection; p95 latency returned to baseline within ~3 minutes after failover.
- No config changes to model runtime or tokenization were made.

Planned actions: 
- CloudMesh will provide incident timeline and coordinate a post-mortem.
- We'll update our routing policies to avoid scheduled control-plane operations during customer high volume windows where possible.
- We propose a 4-hour credit to Sapphire as a goodwill gesture for conversion loss while we complete quantification (finance will follow up).

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-SAPP-4372.docx (draft M.A.P)

Would you be available for a 30-min wrap-up tomorrow 10:30 PT to review the post-mortem and agree on mitigations?

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
